hero.heading: Connecting experienced
hero.description: Together we build a successful study path. The Mentor Programme is a place where experienced students share knowledge and experience with first-year students.

information.title: Learn more
information.programContent: The Mentor Programme is a place where experienced students pass on their knowledge and experience to first-year students. The RSU Mentor Programme for Latvian students is implemented every year from September to February and is based on the principle of volunteering. Its aim is to promote the integration of new students into the academic and social life.
information.mentorContent: A Mentor is an adviser and helper for first-year students. It is a student who has started studies at least in the second year and is ready to share their knowledge and practical experience with new students. A Mentor can give advice and answer questions. One mentor can have up to 5 mentees.
information.menteeContent: Any first-year student can become a mentee. A Mentee is a student who wants to learn about the study process, opportunities for social life at the university, and wants to gain new contacts and experience.

testimonial.title: What participants say
testimonial.quote1:
When I began my studies, everything felt new and unfamiliar. I know how uncertain a first-year student can feel in a new environment — which is exactly why, in my own first year, I signed up for a mentor, and it turned out to be a huge help.
I believe the mentor programme is a wonderful way to give back and to multiply the good. Each of us has been helped during our studies by someone with a piece of wise advice or a supportive shoulder, so it's important that we offer that support to others too, because we ourselves remember so well how it felt in those first days of study.
testimonial.attribution1: — Madara Millere, Faculty of Health and Sports Sciences
testimonial.quote2: The mentor programme at Rīga Stradiņš University, for me, is associated with inspiration and support. I remember my own first semester at university — everything was completely different from secondary school. You don't know anyone, every class is in a different location, and your head is full of so many questions… My mentor inspired me to become the person who helps new students settle into the university environment, so already in my second year of medical studies I became a mentor to 4 mentees. It was important to me to be someone they could turn to confidently at any moment, helping them settle into the RSU environment, understand the nuances of each subject, and feel more secure as they began their studies! That's exactly why I strongly recommend applying — this can become one of the most valuable experiences at the start of your studies.
testimonial.quote3: Before the start of my first year, I knew I wasn't ready and didn't know what to expect from university — from its environment, its studies, and how to find my way around it at all. It was the mentor programme that helped me settle in and realise that you're not alone at university. My mentor was someone I could turn to both with serious questions about my studies and simply for everyday advice. That gave me far greater confidence and motivation. Now I too am the person who helps other students feel more secure, settle into the new environment more easily, and enjoy their time studying not only academically, but also on a human level.
testimonial.attribution3: — Veronika Tagijeva, Faculty of Health and Sports Sciences
testimonial.quote4:
My name is Eduards Doroņins, and I am now in my fourth year studying at the Latvian Academy of Sport Education at RSU. I became a mentor because I remember my own first year of studies well — everything was new and unfamiliar, and there was a lot I had to learn on my own, often by making mistakes. That's exactly why I want to help new students settle into the university environment more easily.

As a mentor, I'm someone you can turn to for advice or help. I introduce students to the RSU and LSPA environment and to student life, and I'm simply available whenever support is needed.

What has especially stayed with me is that both of my mentees became their group leaders. That shows they gained confidence and felt they belonged in the environment.

Mentoring, for me, means the chance to help others grow while gaining valuable experience myself.
